clue.text: Labour-shunning folk carrying Independent — they're seeking depth, not afraid to be wet?

definitions.text: they're seeking depth, not afraid to be wet?

indicators.note: the shirkers carry the next piece within them, so it goes inside

parts.note: skivers are people who dodge work, a British colloquialism
IND is the standard abbreviation for Independent, as in politics

explanation.surface: A sneer at idle people backing an independent candidate, then a jokey picture of people who dive deep and don't mind water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour-shunning' reads as political, but it just means work-shy; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers who swim underwater without suits go down into the depths and plainly expect a soaking, a playful descriptive definition.

clue.text: Type looked for on the radio

indicators.note: something broadcast on the radio is only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: looked for means sought

explanation.surface: Someone tuning a radio hunting for a particular kind of programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A type and a sort are synonyms, both meaning a kind or category.

clue.text: A preparer of tea endlessly refusing to work

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement
without its end, the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A tea-maker who keeps declining to do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of 'refusing', leaving REFUSIN, which 'to work' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An infuser is a small strainer or device holding leaves while they steep, so it literally prepares the brew.

clue.text: Thin disguise failed and Democrat saw the difference

indicators.note: the disguise has broken down, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A politician spots through a flimsy disguise that falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To distinguish between things is to perceive how they differ, so the past tense matches seeing a contrast.

clue.text: Slandered if I must be taken in by poor devil

indicators.note: the words are swallowed up by the next piece, so they sit inside it
a poor version of a word is a badly made one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fears being duped by a wretched demon and so having their name blackened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the letters of devil, and 'taken in by' puts IFI inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To vilify someone is to speak abusively and defamatorily of them, the same as to slander.

clue.text: Accumulated some homespun articles on the way back

indicators.note: the run is read going back, from right to left
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: A collection of home-made goods piled up on a return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes PUNAR from 'homespun articles'; 'on the way back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a bill or debts is to build them up, an idiom for amassing.

clue.text: Very dry, yet welcoming the end of winter

indicators.note: welcoming a guest takes them inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: yet and but both mean however

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is wanted

explanation.surface: A season described as very dry, though the close of winter brings something.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the label for the driest sparkling wine such as champagne.

clue.text: 12 about to work out

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to work out a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a note that something is about to be figured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is STIFF UPPER LIP, firmness of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm determination, the quality of the 12 answer, is resolve: steadfast purpose in the face of difficulty.

clue.text: Vagrant with old profession as a bouncer

parts.note: a tramp is a homeless wanderer
one's line is one's trade or line of work

explanation.surface: A homeless man whose former job was working the door at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman; here it is something you bounce on.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is the springy mat people jump up and down on, so it is literally a thing for bouncing.

clue.text: Loud American taken in by genuine rejection

indicators.note: these pieces are absorbed within the next word, so they go inside

parts.note: genuine means real
F stands for forte, loud in musical notation

explanation.surface: A noisy American fooled by an authentic-seeming turn-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a rejection of an offer or request, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Capital and income principally invested in new casino

indicators.note: money invested is put into something, so the letter goes inside
a new version of the word has its letters remade in another order
principally signals the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A financier sinking capital and income into a freshly opened gambling house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CASINO, and the I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus; 'Capital' poses as money in the surface.

clue.text: Gain on the cards and get ready for action

parts.note: to clear a sum is to make it as net profit
decks are packs of playing cards

explanation.surface: A gambler pocketing winnings at cards, then bracing for what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from sailors clearing a ship's decks before battle, meaning to prepare for something demanding.

clue.text: Doggedness seen in argument with superior in error

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the word for a mistake

parts.note: a slip is a small error
a tiff is a petty quarrel
upper means higher or superior

explanation.surface: Persistence shown when someone wrongly quarrels with their boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a firm upper lip is the British ideal of enduring hardship stoically, a form of determined persistence.

clue.text: Few getting hint after super drops regulars

indicators.note: the hint follows the shortened word
the word loses its every other letter, keeping first, third and fifth

parts.note: an inkling is a slight hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: A small number of people gaining a clue after a supervisor lets go of regular staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinkling means a small scattered number, so it stands for a few.

clue.text: Pair oddly going with villains to get canoes

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first and third

parts.note: rogues are dishonest scoundrels

explanation.surface: A strange couple teaming up with crooks to obtain boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a long narrow dugout boat, a kind of canoe used in the Caribbean and Louisiana.

clue.text: Soldiers hand out painful experience

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers in the British army
to deal cards is to hand them out

explanation.surface: Troops distributing something that hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a harrowing trial or a very unpleasant experience.

clue.text: Casual supporter of the monarchy

definitions.meaning: offhand and careless in manner, as in a dismissive attitude
a Royalist backer of Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.definitionFit: Offhand indifference is one sense; the other is the king's side in the seventeenth-century English civil conflict.

clue.text: Popular commercial vehicle carries one to no avail

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the vehicle carries a load inside it, so a letter goes within

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle used for business
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A well-liked delivery van carrying a passenger, all for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something fruitlessly, without success, is the meaning of the phrase; both mean uselessly.

clue.text: Elects to offend after challenging veto

indicators.note: the word for doing wrong comes after the rearranged word
the word is challenged and knocked into a new order

parts.note: to sin is to offend against a moral law

explanation.surface: Voters choosing to cause offence after a contested veto.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote someone in is to choose them by ballot, the same as electing them.

clue.text: Track information on love and cause of disease

indicators.note: in an across answer, one word placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a path is a track
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Following a lead and gathering facts about romance and illness.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a bacterium, virus or other microbe that produces illness.

clue.text: Reports figure moving around bottom of garden

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around a single letter
moving the letters about rearranges them
in a down clue the bottom is the final letter

explanation.surface: Accounts of a shape shifting about at the end of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports here are the bangs of shots; gunfire is the sound of guns being discharged.

clue.text: Area of growth that's a redneck thing, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A wry comment that some patch of land is typical of rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redneck' is American slang for a rural, conservative person.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot where vegetables and herbs are grown for cooking is a place where things grow.

clue.text: Bottle opener vet stocks

indicators.note: the phrase stocks the word, holding it inside its letters

explanation.surface: A vet keeps a bottle opener in supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang having bottle means having courage, the same as having the nerve.

clue.text: Exploit energy in adipose tissue

indicators.note: the letter goes in the word for body tissue

parts.note: adipose tissue is body fat
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An instruction to use the energy stored in body fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb but is the noun, a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring deed, an achievement.

clue.text: Home team resistance shows the person with the lowdown

parts.note: at home means in
a side is a team
R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: A home side's defence revealing who has the inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation who knows the private details has insider knowledge, the lowdown.

clue.text: Incorporated approach for bank

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for Incorporated after a company name
a line can mean an approach or way of tackling something

explanation.surface: A company's strategy for dealing with a financial bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of earth is a slope, and an incline is a sloping surface.

clue.text: Horse backed in front of good crowd

indicators.note: the reversed word comes before the next letter
backed means turned backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse bet on ahead of a good throng of racegoers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people, a crowd or band.

clue.text: Looking back with honour to accept the origins of this royal office

indicators.note: the word takes in the letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: to honour is to respect

indicators.note: the starting letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Reflecting on the past with pride at taking up a post in a royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a review or survey of past events, the act of regarding times gone by.
